GlobalVariables.StudyDescription: Evaluation survey comparing baseline interactive theorem proving against Output-Directed Theorem Proving in Lean 4.

redcap:Surveys.title: ODTP Pilot User Study Evaluation Survey
redcap:Surveys.instructions: Thank you for participating in our Output-Directed Theorem Proving pilot study. Please answer the following questions regarding your experience across the two tasks.
redcap:Surveys.acknowledgement: Thank you! Your feedback has been recorded.

Question.TranslatedText: Participant ID
How would you rate your overall experience with Interactive Theorem Provers (Coq, Lean, Isabelle, etc.)?
Specifically in Lean 4, how familiar are you with its syntax, Mathlib, and tactic vocabulary?
In your normal proof workflow, how often do you rely on LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude) or web search?

ItemDef.Name: tlx_base_mental
ItemDef.redcap:SectionHeader: Part 2: Cognitive Load (NASA-TLX) - Baseline (Free Web & LLMs)

Question.TranslatedText: Mental Demand: How mentally demanding was the baseline task?
Temporal Demand: How hurried or rushed did you feel to finish within 30 minutes?
Self-Rated Performance: How successful do you think you were in completing the proof? (1 = Failure, 7 = Perfect)
Effort: How hard did you have to work to achieve your level of performance?
Frustration: How insecure, discouraged, irritated, or stressed did you feel?

ItemDef.Name: tlx_odtp_mental
ItemDef.redcap:SectionHeader: Part 2: Cognitive Load (NASA-TLX) - Treatment (ODTP Tool Only)

Question.TranslatedText: Mental Demand: How mentally demanding was the ODTP tool task?
Temporal Demand: How hurried or rushed did you feel to finish within 30 minutes?
Self-Rated Performance: How successful do you think you were in completing the proof? (1 = Failure, 7 = Perfect)
Effort: How hard did you have to work to achieve your level of performance?
Frustration: How insecure, discouraged, irritated, or stressed did you feel?
I felt I had a clear overview of the high-level proof structure at all times (Baseline).
When a proof step succeeded, I clearly understood why it worked mathematically (Baseline).
I spent more time thinking about high-level math strategy rather than fighting syntax or tactic names (Baseline).

ItemDef.Name: und_odtp_overview
ItemDef.redcap:SectionHeader: Part 3: Understanding & Proof Structure - ODTP Tool

Question.TranslatedText: I felt I had a clear overview of the high-level proof structure at all times (ODTP Tool).
When a proof step succeeded, I clearly understood why it worked mathematically (ODTP Tool).
I spent more time thinking about high-level math strategy rather than fighting syntax or tactic names (ODTP Tool).
How did your understanding of the theorem's proof steps differ between using the ODTP tool vs. searching the internet / prompting an external LLM?
When I encountered a roadblock, it was easy to identify what was blocking progress (Baseline).
When I encountered a roadblock, it was easy to identify what was blocking progress (ODTP Tool).
I was able to recover quickly from dead ends or incorrect directions (Baseline).
I was able to recover quickly from dead ends or incorrect directions (ODTP Tool).
Describe a specific moment during either task where you felt completely stuck. What caused you to get stuck, and what helped you get unstuck (or kept you stuck)?

ItemDef.Name: odtp_direct_manip
ItemDef.redcap:SectionHeader: Part 5: ODTP Tool Collaboration & Agency (Treatment Condition)

Question.TranslatedText: Direct Manipulation: Editing the proof state directly (output-directed) felt more intuitive than constructing tactic commands manually.
Cognitive Alignment: The tactics synthesized by the agent matched the mathematical steps I had envisioned in my head.
Division of Labor: I felt in control of the high-level strategy (identifying subproblems/lemmas), while the tool handled syntactic execution.
Trust & Transparency: I trusted the suggestions made by the agent without needing to audit them extensively.
When the agent proposed a tactic that you rejected or had to modify, why did you reject it? (e.g., solved wrong goal, unnatural syntax, took the proof in an undesirable direction)
Which condition allowed you to make progress faster?
If you were formalizing proofs in Lean tomorrow, which approach would you prefer?
What was the single most frustrating or unintuitive part of using the ODTP tool?
What was the single most helpful or powerful part of using the ODTP tool?
